title: How Ruben Hassid built a viral LinkedIn system: be useful, not personal
summary: Ruben explains his content philosophy: optimize for usefulness over personal story, write for a distracted reader on a bus, and post consistently without expecting ROI. He also covers using AI to be "greater, not lazier" through taste and volume, and how EasyGen and his own team's growth became its best marketing.

principles.text: Be useful, not personal: no one cares about your story, so solve a problem for the reader.
principles.quote: always tell my team, now I have a team, be useful, not personal. I am obsessed about being useful.

principles.text: Write for a distracted reader: get them the context and a payoff within seconds, with no long intros.
principles.quote: if within 15 seconds he's not already giving getting something, I'm probably not respecting him. So, no long introduction. I go straight to the point.

principles.text: Every post should leave the reader able to do something better; skip posts that add nothing.
principles.quote: If a post doesn't bring anything, why am I even sharing it? I'm not trying to fill up a calendar of stuff.

principles.text: Use AI to be greater, not lazier: taste and experience plus huge volume of generations beat one-click output.
principles.quote: Am I using it to be lazier or to be greater?

principles.text: Post consistently and don't expect ROI; opportunities come from being useful every day.
principles.quote: If your motivation is to be useful every day on social media, crazy stuff's going to happen because people start to um to see it.

principles.text: Prove the product by using it yourself and with your team; employees who grew with it became top affiliates.
principles.quote: My two biggest affiliates by far are my employees.
